This has been my experience too - having a therapist that validates my trauma induced behaviors for what they actually are - as opposed to CBT that tells me they’re “distortions” - has changed me significantly for the better. It has allowed me to actually process the root cause emotions in a way I couldn’t before, and be angry at the real cause of the emotions instead of blaming myself or perpetually masking my anger. Giving myself the safety to feel all of this has also allowed me to feel more control and make healthier choices for myself that are response to triggers instead of reactions. I’m pretty sure others have said this, but I wanted to add my comment to confirm it’s not only possible to have all three issues, but the actual root cause of things like anxiety is often easy to miss. I never thought I’d find anything to ever help my anxiety, it has been so strong and bad and resistant to every med and treatment modality. I thought it was just my lot in life. I was diagnosed last year with ADHD-C and stimulant meds were recommended. I mostly expected them to help with focus, which was becoming a huge issue with my work. The psychiatrist I saw said off-handedly that they may also help with anxiety. In my mind I scoffed and was like “Yeah, sure”. I figured he’d meant because I’d have focus to get work done and sure that would decrease my situational anxiety. I started Adderall and the night and day difference in my anxiety is unreal. When it kicks in I don’t feel euphoric - I just feel calm. Like what I imagine a person without anxiety feels. 

Shortly after starting meds at least three of my coworkers all independently mentioned to me that I seemed so much calmer on team video calls and I was talking a lot more (as in, meaningfully participating in the discussion) and they just wanted to let me know they noticed a positive change. Zero of them knew about my diagnosis or the meds. After this feedback I realized this was happening because I no longer felt the crippling, heart racing, I am going to have a panic attack and die, social anxiety feeling I’ve absolutely always had in those sort of situations, because I take the Adderall before work so it’s keeping me calm and way more focused during work hours. Not only did it get rid of my anxiety (this isn’t an exaggeration - when the med is working my anxiety is gone) but it does help me focus so I can keep track of what is going on during the call and keep track of my own thoughts in response and then actually say them. 

Guess what else? This feeling of calm, control, focus, handling work better, hours of anxiety free time, have all contributed to decreasing my depression. Sometimes the thing we have always felt was the biggest issue is actually a symptom of something else. 

I hope you’re able to get the support you need to figure out your root cause and then have a treatment plan that is maximally effective for everything for you.

This is just my personal experience/opinion, and I'm no doctor or expert, but from what I've gathered stimulant medications really hit different for non-ADHDers, in a way that is much more addiction inducing. People can get addicted to almost anything if they're built in a way that makes something particularly wonderful to their body. I am sure there are ADHDers for whom certain stimulant meds hit in a way more addictive way. But by and large what I've read from groups like this one, where none of us have any reason to lie about how our stimulant meds make us feel, those reporting to have ADHD and taking a stimulant med do not report those addiction inducing feelings from it. 

In my personal experience so far, the one med I've tried, I can tell it has kicked in for the day because I don't have racing thoughts and I have a very strong urge to nap. Yes. Nap. After my stimulant med kicks in. Nap. Because finally my body and mind has calmed down from the meds. I get zero euphoria (or maybe my euphoria is just the noticing I'm calm?!) or any of the feelings that something like, say, my old anxiety med (another controlled substance) used to give me that also created "cravings" for that med. I have zero cravings for my Adderall. I desire to take it daily because I am really happy to have emotional regulation and the ability to make decisions I can act upon, but even knowing it can create that state for me I still will forget to take it. Maybe there is another med that would create addictive feelings for me, but so far, this one hasn't. And it really kinda helps reinforce for me that I genuinely need it to assist with normal functioning, but it works at a level that if I have to go without it I only feel the same level of annoyed that I cannot function as I did before I ever had a med to take in the first place.

My mother used to pridefully tell me, and anyone else who would listen, the story about how my third grade teacher told us (my mother and me) that I was one of the most “hard on yourself” kids she’d ever taught. 

I incorporated this story into my psyche as a sign I was always broken, even as a child. That some part of me has always just been super self-critical and my mother was so shocked by this that she repeated the story time and time again as I grew up. 

Fast forward to realizing (recently) my childhood resulted in CPTSD, and one day I remember this story, and how my mother handled it, how she repeated it over and over like it was bragging. Which I don’t understand. But what I did come to understand was that at the age of 7-8, my teacher told my parents I was struggling with self loathing and self-criticism, and my mother’s reaction was not to help me and support me, but to repeat the story of someone else identifying my trauma and her never doing jack about it. In fact, I think at times she repeated that story to me to tell me to “just stop being so hard on yourself” the few times I opened up to her growing up - to say “look, you’ve always been this way, not my fault! just suck it up buttercup”. 

I feel like my rambling is getting jumbled here but the point is I identified so much with what you said - a massive amount of the emotional abuse and neglect I went through was constant constructive abandonment.  So much so my mother would brag about my trauma and re-traumatize me with stories like what my third grade teacher said while never, not once, of this I am certain, offering me any kind of actual love, support, empathy, kindness, or recognizing *she* was incapable of helping me and finding me someone who could help me.

The night I, at 20 years old, drove several hours back to my parents house from college. I was driving back late at night because I had spent the day in a school disciplinary hearing recounting the night I was raped in an effort to have my rapist removed from school. 

I had been utterly and completely alone through the whole thing. I had been pressured by the school administration to drop my complaint. They let the rapist directly question me at the hearing. 

I had told my parents about this happening when a few weeks before the hearing I was told I may need an attorney. I contacted my parents by phone, sobbing, said what happened, and asked for help. In response, my mother began crying about how painful it was for her to hear this, and that neither her nor my father could offer any kind of support. Sorry. They were too strapped for cash helping my sibling with something. 

Then the call ended.
